  2850	A foundation with no manuscript label of its own; everything is proved and
  2851	nothing is supplied. It is the finite Gaussian Fock layer used in
  2852	`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420` (main TeX):
  2853	the Fock half of the proof of `L:fock-form` (lines 2515-2526), the Fock
  2854	sentences of the proof of `L:interval-contractions` (lines 2887-2891), the
  2855	phase insertion on a color in its vacuum (lines 2838-2841 and 2878-2880),
  2856	and the Hermite step of `E:occupied-multiplication` (lines 1805-1810). The
  2857	TeX cites Janson (lines 2467-2468) for the creation and annihilation
  2858	algebra; this module proves what is used.
  2859	
  2860	Model (decision 5 of wave L9). The Gaussian `L^2` space with values in a
  2861	complex inner product space `X` is represented by coefficient vectors
  2862	`(Fin m -> N) -> X`, indexed by multi-indices, restricted to total degree
  2863	at most `N` (`degLE m N`; `Supp N v` says `v` vanishes above degree `N`).
  2864	The expansion `iota N v (x) = sum_(|k| <= N) h_k(x) v_k` in the normalized
  2865	Hermite functions of `GaussianHermite` links the two pictures: it is an
  2866	isometry into `L^2(stdPi m; X)` (`integral_norm_sq_iota`; `stdPi m` is the
  2867	law of `m` independent standard Gaussians), multiplication by `x_i` is
  2868	`a_i^* + a_i` on coefficients (`coord_smul_iota`), and `sum_i x_i H_i` is
  2869	the field operator `fieldOp H` (`sum_coord_smul_iota`). No tensor-product
  2870	inner product is used: the "other Hilbert factor" of the TeX is `X` itself,
  2871	and the spatial operators `H_i` are continuous linear maps of `X`. The TeX
  2872	rotates `H/||H||` to a first coordinate (line 1805); the general column
  2873	form with operators `H_i` makes that step unnecessary.
  2874	
  2875	Formalized. The annihilation and creation operators
  2876	`(a_i v)_k = sqrt(k_i+1) v_(k+e_i)`, `(a_i^* v)_k = sqrt(k_i) v_(k-e_i)`,
  2877	the number identity `sum_i a_i^* a_i = |k|`, and the finite adjoint
  2878	identity between `a_i` and `a_i^*`. The creation row from degrees `<= N` to
  2879	degrees `<= N+1` has norm at most `sqrt(N+1)` (`creRow_bound`), attained on
  2880	`u_i = a_i w` for `w` of exact degree `N+1` (`creRow_attained`). For
  2881	symmetric `H_1, ..., H_m` with the column bound
  2882	`sum_i ||H_i u||^2 <= c ||u||^2`, `c >= 0` (hypotheses of these lemmas, not
  2883	manuscript inputs here), the field operator `sum_i (a_i^* + a_i) (x) H_i`
  2884	maps degrees `<= N` to degrees `<= N+1` with norm at most
  2885	`2 sqrt(N+1) sqrt(c)` (`fieldOp_bound`), the same after truncation to
  2886	degrees `<= N` (`fieldOp_bound_trunc`), the truncated operator is symmetric
  2887	(`fieldOp_symm_trunc`), and both bounds hold in Gaussian `L^2` with
  2888	integrability (`gaussian_field_bound`, `gaussian_field_bound_trunc`).
  2889	Vacuum insertion: `E||sum_i g_i w_i||^2 = sum_i ||w_i||^2`
  2890	(`vacuum_insertion_isometry`).
  2891	
  2892	Route difference. The TeX bounds the annihilation part as the adjoint of
  2893	the creation part (line 2522); Lean uses the same adjoint relation through
  2894	the finite identity `sum_inner_ann` and Cauchy-Schwarz, which gives the
  2895	annihilation bound `(N+1) c` rather than the TeX's `N c` (line 1808 states
  2896	`sqrt(n)` for the annihilation norm). The constant `4(N+1)c` of the sum does
  2897	not need the sharper value.
  2898	
  2899	Junk values. The truncated subtraction `k - e_i` occurs only multiplied by
  2900	`sqrt(k_i)`, which vanishes exactly when it truncates; `c >= 0` is a
  2901	hypothesis where it is used; every integral conclusion includes
  2902	integrability. Coefficient vectors are arbitrary functions; only their
  2903	values in degrees `<= N` (or `<= N+1`) enter the stated sums.
  2904	
  2905	Not formalized here: the full Gaussian `L^2` space, infinitely many
  2906	coordinates, the closed polynomial spaces and unbounded number operators.
  2907

  2909	`N` in place of `N+1` in `creRow_bound` fails at the vacuum), `NumberOrder`

2910	(`|k| + 1` in place of `|k|` in `number_identity`) and `VacuumSquareOfSum`
  2911	(`(sum_i ||w_i||)^2` in place of `sum_i ||w_i||^2` in

    18	inner product space `X` is represented on the finite coefficient spaces
    19	`(Fin m → ℕ) → X` indexed by multi-indices of total degree at most `N`
    20	(`degLE m N`), through the expansion `iota N v x = ∑_{|k| ≤ N} hk_k(x) v_k` in
    21	the normalized Hermite functions of `GaussianHermite`.  No tensor-product inner
    22	product is used; the "other Hilbert factor" of the TeX is `X` itself.
    23	
    24	Contents (everything proved, nothing supplied):
    25	* the creation and annihilation operators on coefficients,
    26	  `(a_i v)_k = √(k_i+1) v_{k+e_i}`, `(a_i^* v)_k = √(k_i) v_{k-e_i}`
    27	  (`ann`, `cre`), and multiplication by `g_i`, `gmul i = a_i^* + a_i`;
    28	* the number identity `∑_i a_i^* a_i = |k|` on the coefficient of index `k`
    29	  (`number_identity`), and the adjoint relation between `a_i` and `a_i^*`
    30	  (`sum_inner_ann`);
    31	* the creation row `(u_i) ↦ ∑_i a_i^* u_i` from degrees `≤ j` to degrees
    32	  `≤ j+1` has norm at most `√(j+1)` (`creRow_bound`), attained on
    33	  `u_i = a_i w` for `w` of exact degree `j+1` (`creRow_attained`);
    34	* for `H_1, …, H_m` symmetric (self-adjoint) operators on `X` with
    35	  `∑_i ‖H_i u‖² ≤ c ‖u‖²`, the field operator `∑_i (a_i^* + a_i) ⊗ H_i`
    36	  (`fieldOp`) maps degrees `≤ N` to degrees `≤ N+1` with norm at most
    37	  `2√(N+1)√c`, untruncated (`fieldOp_bound`) and after truncation to degrees
    38	  `≤ N` (`fieldOp_bound_trunc`); the truncated operator is symmetric
    39	  (`fieldOp_symm_trunc`);
    40	* the Gaussian side: the expansion is an isometry
    41	  (`integral_norm_sq_iota`), multiplication by the coordinate `x_i` is `gmul i`
    42	  on coefficients (`coord_smul_iota`), and `∑_i x_i H_i` acting on `iota N v`
    43	  is `iota (N+1) (fieldOp H v)` (`sum_coord_smul_iota`), so the two Fock bounds
    44	  are bounds for Gaussian `L²(X)` norms (`gaussian_field_bound`,
    45	  `gaussian_field_bound_trunc`);
    46	* vacuum insertion: `∫ ‖∑_i x_i w_i‖² dγ_m = ∑_i ‖w_i‖²`
    47	  (`vacuum_insertion_isometry`).
    48	
    49	Route difference: the TeX bounds the annihilation part as the adjoint of the
    50	creation part; here the same adjoint relation is used through the finite
    51	identity `sum_inner_ann` and Cauchy-Schwarz, giving the annihilation bound
    52	`(N+1)c` (the TeX's `N c` is not needed for the constant `4(N+1)c`).  The TeX
    53	rotates `H/‖H‖` to the first coordinate; the general column form with
    54	operators `H_i` makes that step unnecessary.
    55	
    56	Junk values: the truncated subtraction `k - e_i` occurs only multiplied by
    57	`√(k_i)`, which vanishes exactly when it truncates; `c ≥ 0` is a hypothesis
    58	where it is used; every integral conclusion includes integrability.
    59	-/

    77	/-! ### Multi-indices -/
    78	
    79	/-- The total degree `|k| = ∑_i k_i` of a multi-index. -/
    80	def deg (k : Fin m → ℕ) : ℕ := ∑ i, k i
    81	
    82	/-- The multi-indices of total degree at most `N`. -/
    83	def degLE (m N : ℕ) : Finset (Fin m → ℕ) :=
    84	  (Fintype.piFinset fun _ => range (N + 1)).filter fun k => ∑ i, k i ≤ N
    85	
    86	/-- Membership in `degLE m N` is `|k| ≤ N`. -/
    87	theorem mem_degLE {N : ℕ} {k : Fin m → ℕ} : k ∈ degLE m N ↔ deg k ≤ N := by
    88	  simp only [degLE, mem_filter, Fintype.mem_piFinset, mem_range, deg]
    89	  refine ⟨fun h => h.2, fun h => ⟨fun i => ?_, h⟩⟩
    90	  have := Finset.single_le_sum (fun j _ => Nat.zero_le (k j)) (mem_univ i)
    91	  omega
    92	
    93	/-- Auxiliary: `degLE m N ⊆ degLE m M` for `N ≤ M`. -/
    94	theorem degLE_mono {N M : ℕ} (h : N ≤ M) : degLE m N ⊆ degLE m M :=
    95	  fun _ hk => mem_degLE.2 ((mem_degLE.1 hk).trans h)
    96	
    97	/-- Auxiliary: `0 ∈ degLE m N`. -/
    98	theorem zero_mem_degLE (N : ℕ) : (0 : Fin m → ℕ) ∈ degLE m N := mem_degLE.2 (by simp [deg])
    99	
   100	/-- Auxiliary: `|k + e_i| = |k| + 1`. -/
   101	theorem deg_add_unitIdx (k : Fin m → ℕ) (i : Fin m) : deg (k + unitIdx i) = deg k + 1 := by
   102	  simp [deg, Finset.sum_add_distrib, unitIdx]
   103	
   104	/-- Auxiliary: `(k - e_i) + e_i = k` when `k_i ≠ 0`. -/
   105	theorem sub_add_unitIdx {k : Fin m → ℕ} {i : Fin m} (h : k i ≠ 0) :
   106	    k - unitIdx i + unitIdx i = k := by
   107	  funext j
   108	  by_cases hj : j = i
   109	  · subst hj; simp; omega
   110	  · simp [unitIdx, hj]
   111	
   112	/-- Auxiliary: `(k + e_i) - e_i = k`. -/
   113	theorem add_sub_unitIdx (k : Fin m → ℕ) (i : Fin m) : k + unitIdx i - unitIdx i = k := by
   114	  funext j; simp
   115	
   116	/-- Auxiliary: `|k - e_i| + 1 = |k|` when `k_i ≠ 0`. -/
   117	theorem deg_sub_unitIdx {k : Fin m → ℕ} {i : Fin m} (h : k i ≠ 0) :
   118	    deg (k - unitIdx i) + 1 = deg k := by
   119	  conv_rhs => rw [← sub_add_unitIdx h]
   120	  rw [deg_add_unitIdx]
   121	
   122	/-- Auxiliary: `(k - e_i)_i = k_i - 1`. -/
   123	theorem sub_unitIdx_apply (k : Fin m → ℕ) (i : Fin m) : (k - unitIdx i) i = k i - 1 := by
   124	  simp
   125	
   126	/-- Auxiliary: `(k + e_i)_i = k_i + 1`. -/
   127	theorem add_unitIdx_apply (k : Fin m → ℕ) (i : Fin m) : (k + unitIdx i) i = k i + 1 := by
   128	  simp
   129	
   130	/-- Auxiliary (reindexing): a function vanishing on `k_i = 0`, summed over
   131	degrees `≤ N+1`, equals its shift by `e_i` summed over degrees `≤ N`. -/
   132	theorem sum_degLE_succ_eq (i : Fin m) (N : ℕ) {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M]
   133	    (g : (Fin m → ℕ) → M) (hg : ∀ k, k i = 0 → g k = 0) :
   134	    ∑ k ∈ degLE m (N + 1), g k = ∑ j ∈ degLE m N, g (j + unitIdx i) := by
   135	  classical
   136	  rw [← Finset.sum_filter_of_ne (p := fun k => k i ≠ 0) (fun k _ hne h0 => hne (hg k h0))]
   137	  symm
   138	  refine Finset.sum_nbij' (fun j => j + unitIdx i) (fun k => k - unitIdx i) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
   139	  · intro j hj
   140	    simp only [mem_filter] at hj ⊢
   141	    refine ⟨mem_degLE.2 ?_, by simp⟩
   142	    rw [deg_add_unitIdx]; have := mem_degLE.1 hj; omega
   143	  · intro k hk
   144	    simp only [mem_filter] at hk ⊢
   145	    have h1 := deg_sub_unitIdx hk.2
   146	    have h2 := mem_degLE.1 hk.1
   147	    exact mem_degLE.2 (by omega)
   148	  · intro j _; exact add_sub_unitIdx j i
   149	  · intro k hk
   150	    simp only [mem_filter] at hk
   151	    exact sub_add_unitIdx hk.2
   152	  · intro j _; rfl
   153	
   154	/-- Auxiliary: a function vanishing in degrees above `N` has the same sum over
   155	`degLE m M` for every `M ≥ N`. -/
   156	theorem sum_degLE_eq_of_vanish {N M : ℕ} (hNM : N ≤ M) {E : Type*} [AddCommMonoid E]
   157	    (g : (Fin m → ℕ) → E) (hg : ∀ k, N < deg k → g k = 0) :
   158	    ∑ k ∈ degLE m M, g k = ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, g k := by
   159	  symm
   160	  refine Finset.sum_subset (degLE_mono hNM) fun k _ hk => hg k ?_
   161	  rw [mem_degLE] at hk; omega

   163	/-! ### Coefficient operators -/
   164	
   165	variable {X : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [InnerProductSpace ℂ X]
   166	
   167	/-- A coefficient vector vanishes in degrees above `N`. -/
   168	def Supp (N : ℕ) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) : Prop := ∀ k, N < deg k → v k = 0
   169	
   170	/-- The annihilation operator `(a_i v)_k = √(k_i+1) v_{k+e_i}`. -/
   171	def ann (i : Fin m) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) (k : Fin m → ℕ) : X :=
   172	  (Real.sqrt ((k i : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ) • v (k + unitIdx i)
   173	
   174	/-- The creation operator `(a_i^* v)_k = √(k_i) v_{k-e_i}`. -/
   175	def cre (i : Fin m) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) (k : Fin m → ℕ) : X :=
   176	  (Real.sqrt (k i : ℝ) : ℂ) • v (k - unitIdx i)
   177	
   178	/-- Multiplication by the coordinate `g_i` on coefficients, `a_i^* + a_i`. -/
   179	def gmul (i : Fin m) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) (k : Fin m → ℕ) : X := cre i v k + ann i v k
   180	
   181	/-- The creation row `(u_i)_i ↦ ∑_i a_i^* u_i`. -/
   182	def creRow (u : Fin m → (Fin m → ℕ) → X) (k : Fin m → ℕ) : X := ∑ i, cre i (u i) k
   183	
   184	/-- The field operator `∑_i (a_i^* + a_i) ⊗ H_i` on coefficients. -/
   185	def fieldOp (H : Fin m → X →L[ℂ] X) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) (k : Fin m → ℕ) : X :=
   186	  ∑ i, gmul i (fun l => H i (v l)) k
   187	
   188	/-- The vacuum vector `1 ⊗ u` (coefficient `u` at `k = 0`). -/
   189	def vac (u : X) : (Fin m → ℕ) → X := fun k => if k = 0 then u else 0
   190	
   191	/-- Auxiliary: `(a_i^* v)_k = 0` when `k_i = 0`. -/
   192	theorem cre_of_eq_zero (i : Fin m) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) {k : Fin m → ℕ} (h : k i = 0) :
   193	    cre i v k = 0 := by simp [cre, h]
   194	
   195	/-- `a_i^* a_i` multiplies the coefficient of index `k` by `k_i`. -/
   196	theorem cre_ann (i : Fin m) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) (k : Fin m → ℕ) :
   197	    cre i (ann i v) k = ((k i : ℝ) : ℂ) • v k := by
   198	  unfold cre ann
   199	  by_cases h : k i = 0
   200	  · simp [h]
   201	  · rw [sub_add_unitIdx h, smul_smul, ← Complex.ofReal_mul, sub_unitIdx_apply]
   202	    have : ((k i - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1 = k i := by
   203	      rw [Nat.cast_sub (by omega)]; ring
   204	    rw [this, Real.mul_self_sqrt (Nat.cast_nonneg _)]
   205	
   206	/-- **Number identity** `∑_i a_i^* a_i = |k|` on the coefficient of index `k`. -/
   207	theorem number_identity (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) (k : Fin m → ℕ) :
   208	    ∑ i, cre i (ann i v) k = ((deg k : ℝ) : ℂ) • v k := by
   209	  simp only [cre_ann, ← Finset.sum_smul, deg]
   210	  push_cast; rfl
   211	
   212	/-- **Adjoint relation** of `a_i` and `a_i^*`:
   213	`∑_{|k| ≤ N} ⟨(a_i v)_k, w_k⟩ = ∑_{|k| ≤ N+1} ⟨v_k, (a_i^* w)_k⟩`. -/
   214	theorem sum_inner_ann (i : Fin m) (N : ℕ) (v w : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) :
   215	    ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, inner ℂ (ann i v k) (w k) =
   216	      ∑ k ∈ degLE m (N + 1), inner ℂ (v k) (cre i w k) := by
   217	  rw [sum_degLE_succ_eq i N (fun k => inner ℂ (v k) (cre i w k))
   218	    (fun k hk => by simp [cre_of_eq_zero i w hk])]
   219	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => ?_
   220	  simp only [ann, cre, add_unitIdx_apply, add_sub_unitIdx, inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right,

221	    Complex.conj_ofReal]
   222	  push_cast; ring
   223	
   224	/-- The conjugate form of `sum_inner_ann`. -/
   225	theorem sum_inner_cre (i : Fin m) (N : ℕ) (v w : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) :
   226	    ∑ k ∈ degLE m (N + 1), inner ℂ (cre i v k) (w k) =
   227	      ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, inner ℂ (v k) (ann i w k) := by
   228	  have h := congrArg (starRingEnd ℂ) (sum_inner_ann i N w v)
   229	  simp only [map_sum, inner_conj_symm] at h
   230	  exact h.symm

   232	/-! ### Norm bounds -/
   233	
   234	/-- Auxiliary: `(∑ re⟨x_k, y_k⟩)² ≤ (∑ ‖x_k‖²)(∑ ‖y_k‖²)` when the left sum
   235	is nonnegative. -/
   236	theorem sq_sum_re_inner_le {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (x y : ι → X)
   237	    (h0 : 0 ≤ ∑ k ∈ s, RCLike.re (inner ℂ (x k) (y k))) :
   238	    (∑ k ∈ s, RCLike.re (inner ℂ (x k) (y k))) ^ 2 ≤
   239	      (∑ k ∈ s, ‖x k‖ ^ 2) * ∑ k ∈ s, ‖y k‖ ^ 2 := by
   240	  have h1 : ∑ k ∈ s, RCLike.re (inner ℂ (x k) (y k)) ≤ ∑ k ∈ s, ‖x k‖ * ‖y k‖ :=
   241	    Finset.sum_le_sum fun k _ => re_inner_le_norm _ _
   242	  calc _ ≤ (∑ k ∈ s, ‖x k‖ * ‖y k‖) ^ 2 := pow_le_pow_left₀ h0 h1 2
   243	    _ ≤ _ := Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq s _ _
   244	
   245	/-- **Creation-row bound**: `(u_i) ↦ ∑_i a_i^* u_i` from degrees `≤ N` to
   246	degrees `≤ N+1` has norm at most `√(N+1)`, in the form
   247	`∑_{|k| ≤ N+1} ‖∑_i (a_i^* u_i)_k‖² ≤ (N+1) ∑_i ∑_{|j| ≤ N} ‖u_{i,j}‖²`. -/
   248	theorem creRow_bound (N : ℕ) (u : Fin m → (Fin m → ℕ) → X) :
   249	    ∑ k ∈ degLE m (N + 1), ‖creRow u k‖ ^ 2 ≤
   250	      ((N : ℝ) + 1) * ∑ i, ∑ j ∈ degLE m N, ‖u i j‖ ^ 2 := by
   251	  classical
   252	  set g : Fin m → (Fin m → ℕ) → ℝ := fun i k => if k i = 0 then 0 else ‖u i (k - unitIdx i)‖
   253	  have hpt : ∀ k ∈ degLE m (N + 1), ‖creRow u k‖ ^ 2 ≤ ((N : ℝ) + 1) * ∑ i, g i k ^ 2 := by
   254	    intro k hk
   255	    have h1 : ‖creRow u k‖ ≤ ∑ i, Real.sqrt (k i) * g i k := by
   256	      refine (norm_sum_le _ _).trans (Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => ?_)
   257	      by_cases h : k i = 0
   258	      · simp [cre, h, g]
   259	      · simp only [cre, norm_smul, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs, g, h, ↓reduceIte,
   260	          abs_of_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)]
   261	        exact le_rfl
   262	    have h2 := Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq univ (fun i => Real.sqrt (k i)) (g · k)
   263	    have h3 : ∑ i, Real.sqrt (k i : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ (N : ℝ) + 1 := by
   264	      simp only [Real.sq_sqrt (Nat.cast_nonneg _)]
   265	      have := mem_degLE.1 hk
   266	      exact_mod_cast (show deg k ≤ N + 1 from this)
   267	    calc ‖creRow u k‖ ^ 2 ≤ (∑ i, Real.sqrt (k i) * g i k) ^ 2 :=
   268	          pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _) h1 2
   269	      _ ≤ _ := h2.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right h3
   270	          (Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ => sq_nonneg _))
   271	  refine (Finset.sum_le_sum hpt).trans ?_
   272	  rw [← Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_comm]
   273	  refine mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (le_of_eq (Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_)) (by positivity)
   274	  rw [sum_degLE_succ_eq i N (fun k => g i k ^ 2) (fun k hk => by simp [g, hk])]
   275	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => ?_
   276	  simp [g]
   277	
   278	/-- The creation part `∑_i a_i^* ⊗ H_i` of the field operator. -/
   279	def creOp (H : Fin m → X →L[ℂ] X) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) (k : Fin m → ℕ) : X :=
   280	  creRow (fun i l => H i (v l)) k
   281	
   282	/-- The annihilation part `∑_i a_i ⊗ H_i` of the field operator. -/
   283	def annOp (H : Fin m → X →L[ℂ] X) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) (k : Fin m → ℕ) : X :=
   284	  ∑ i, ann i (fun l => H i (v l)) k
   285	
   286	/-- The field operator is the sum of its creation and annihilation parts. -/
   287	theorem fieldOp_eq (H : Fin m → X →L[ℂ] X) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) (k : Fin m → ℕ) :
   288	    fieldOp H v k = creOp H v k + annOp H v k := by
   289	  simp [fieldOp, creOp, annOp, creRow, gmul, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   290	
   291	/-- The creation part with a column bound `∑_i ‖H_i u‖² ≤ c ‖u‖²`:
   292	`∑_{|k| ≤ N+1} ‖(creOp H v)_k‖² ≤ (N+1) c ∑_{|j| ≤ N} ‖v_j‖²`. -/
   293	theorem creOp_bound (N : ℕ) (H : Fin m → X →L[ℂ] X) {c : ℝ}
   294	    (hc : ∀ u, ∑ i, ‖H i u‖ ^ 2 ≤ c * ‖u‖ ^ 2) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) :
   295	    ∑ k ∈ degLE m (N + 1), ‖creOp H v k‖ ^ 2 ≤
   296	      ((N : ℝ) + 1) * c * ∑ j ∈ degLE m N, ‖v j‖ ^ 2 := by
   297	  refine (creRow_bound N _).trans ?_
   298	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   299	  calc ((N : ℝ) + 1) * ∑ j ∈ degLE m N, ∑ i, ‖H i (v j)‖ ^ 2
   300	      ≤ ((N : ℝ) + 1) * ∑ j ∈ degLE m N, c * ‖v j‖ ^ 2 :=
   301	        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (Finset.sum_le_sum fun j _ => hc (v j)) (by positivity)
   302	    _ = _ := by rw [← Finset.mul_sum]; ring
   303	
   304	/-- The annihilation part, for symmetric `H_i` with column bound `c ≥ 0`:
   305	`∑_{|k| ≤ N} ‖(annOp H v)_k‖² ≤ (N+1) c ∑_{|k| ≤ N+1} ‖v_k‖²` (adjoint of the
   306	creation part). -/
   307	theorem annOp_bound (N : ℕ) (H : Fin m → X →L[ℂ] X)
   308	    (hH : ∀ i u w, inner ℂ (H i u) w = inner ℂ u (H i w)) {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 ≤ c)
   309	    (hc : ∀ u, ∑ i, ‖H i u‖ ^ 2 ≤ c * ‖u‖ ^ 2) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) :
   310	    ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, ‖annOp H v k‖ ^ 2 ≤
   311	      ((N : ℝ) + 1) * c * ∑ k ∈ degLE m (N + 1), ‖v k‖ ^ 2 := by
   312	  set a := annOp H v
   313	  set S := ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, ‖a k‖ ^ 2
   314	  set V := ∑ k ∈ degLE m (N + 1), ‖v k‖ ^ 2
   315	  have hS : S = ∑ k ∈ degLE m (N + 1), RCLike.re (inner ℂ (v k) (creOp H a k)) := by
   316	    have e1 : ∀ k, ‖a k‖ ^ 2 = RCLike.re (∑ i, inner ℂ (ann i v k) (H i (a k))) := by
   317	      intro k
   318	      rw [@norm_sq_eq_re_inner ℂ]
   319	      congr 1
   320	      have : inner ℂ (a k) (a k) = ∑ i, inner ℂ (ann i (fun l => H i (v l)) k) (a k) := by
   321	        show inner ℂ (annOp H v k) (a k) = _
   322	        rw [annOp, sum_inner]
   323	      rw [this]
   324	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
   325	      simp only [ann, inner_smul_left, hH]
   326	    simp only [S, e1, ← map_sum]
   327	    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   328	    simp only [sum_inner_ann]
   329	    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   330	    congr 1
   331	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun k _ => ?_
   332	    rw [creOp, creRow, inner_sum]
   333	  have hS0 : 0 ≤ S := Finset.sum_nonneg fun k _ => sq_nonneg _
   334	  have hsq : S ^ 2 ≤ V * (((N : ℝ) + 1) * c * S) := by
   335	    have := sq_sum_re_inner_le (degLE m (N + 1)) v (creOp H a) (hS ▸ hS0)
   336	    rw [← hS] at this
   337	    exact this.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (creOp_bound N H hc a)

    73	 2043| \section{A static phase estimate at first variance order}
    74	 2044| \label{S:static-phase}

    77	 2047| establish a uniform estimate for the first variance coefficient with arbitrary

    79	 2049| three-dimensional class; no endpoint representation is assumed. The estimate
    80	 2050| below is not an all-order propagator bound.

    82	 2052| 
    83	 2053| 
    84	 2054| Let $0 < \alpha < 2$, and let $\Gamma$ be a nonnegative, even, positive-definite
    85	 2055| tempered Radon covariance on $\R^3$, satisfying $\Gamma(rA) =
    86	 2056| r^{3-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$. Its spectral convention is $\Gamma = \int e^{i\xi\cdot
    87	 2057| x}\mu(\ud\xi)$. Put
    88	 2058| \begin{equation}\label{E:phase-constants}
    89	 2059|   \begin{split}

    91	 2061|     R_\alpha=\frac{\alpha\pi V}{2\sin(\pi\alpha/2)},\\
    92	 2062|     c_\Gamma&=\frac{(3-\alpha)M}{4\pi},\qquad
    93	 2063|     b_\alpha=2^\alpha+\frac{3^{2-\alpha}}{2-\alpha},\qquad

    95	 2065|   \end{split}
    96	 2066| \end{equation}

   102	 2072| \begin{lemma}[Two static contraction bounds]\label{L:phase-contractions}

   106	 2076|     &\le R_\alpha\lambda^{\alpha-2},

   108	 2078|     \left|T_\epsilon(a,q)\right|

   111	 2081|     T_\epsilon(a,q)

   291	 2798| These estimates concern individual static phase and interaction maps. Their
   292	 2799| summability alone does not identify the evolution driven by overlapping interval
   293	 2800| fields. The coefficient argument in Section~\ref{S:interval-upper} supplies the
   294	 2801| separate estimate needed for that evolution.

   296	 2803| \section{Interval fields and the full upper bound}
   297	 2804| \label{S:interval-upper}
   298	 2805| 
   299	 2806| The intrinsic constant is identified independently in
   300	 2807| Theorem~\ref{T:intrinsic-second-moment}.

   302	 2809| Write
   303	 2810| \[
   304	 2811|   \nu=3-\alpha>1,\qquad
   305	 2812|   \beta=4-\alpha-\alpha_0>2,\qquad p=2-\alpha_0>1.
   306	 2813| \]
   307	 2814| Thus, $\beta-\nu = 1-\alpha_0 > 0$. In this section the spatial dimension is any
   308	 2815| admissible $d \in \{1,2,3\}$. The spatial covariance is the nonnegative, even,
   309	 2816| positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$, with scaling $\Gamma(rA) =
   310	 2817| r^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$ and spectral convention $\Gamma = \int e^{i\xi\cdot
   311	 2818| x}\mu(\ud\xi)$. This includes $\Gamma = \delta_0$ when $d = \alpha = 1$. Set
   312	 2819| \[
   313	 2820|   R_\alpha=\frac{\alpha\pi\mu(B_1)}{2\sin(\pi\alpha/2)},\qquad
   314	 2821|   A_\rho=\rho^2-\Delta,\qquad
   315	 2822|   \|(f,g)\|_\rho^2=\|f\|_2^2+\|A_\rho^{-1/2}g\|_2^2.
   316	 2823| \]

   319	 2826| \subsection{Contractions and complex phase estimates}
   320	 2827| 
   321	 2828| \begin{lemma}[Dimension-independent Gaussian contractions]
   322	 2829|   \label{L:interval-contractions}
   323	 2830|   Uniformly in positive spatial smoothing and in finite Gaussian-mode and
   324	 2831|   spatial Fourier-band cutoffs,
   325	 2832|   \begin{equation}\label{E:interval-column}
   326	 2833|     \sum_m\|A_\rho^{-1/2}M_{e_m}f\|_2^2
   327	 2834|     \le R_\alpha\rho^{\alpha-2}\|f\|_2^2.
   328	 2835|   \end{equation}
   329	 2836|   Here $W_\epsilon(x) = \sum_m g_me_m(x)$ is an orthonormal-coordinate
   330	 2837|   representation of $W(p_\epsilon(x-\cdot))$, whose covariance is
   331	 2838|   $\Gamma_\epsilon = p_{2\epsilon}*\Gamma$. Consequently, on a Gaussian color
   332	 2839|   that is initially in its vacuum, the phase insertion
   333	 2840|   $(u,v)\mapsto(0,W_\epsilon u)$ has norm at most
   334	 2841|   $\sqrt{R_\alpha}\rho^{(\alpha-2)/2}$ into its Gaussian $L^2$ phase. With
   335	 2842|   Hermite degree of this color truncated at $N$, its sandwiched field has
   336	 2843|   operator norm at most
   337	 2844|   \begin{equation}\label{E:interval-fock}
   338	 2845|     2\sqrt{N+1}\sqrt{R_\alpha}\rho^{\alpha/2-2}.
   339	 2846|   \end{equation}
   340	 2847|   Both statements remain valid tensoring with any other Hilbert factor.
   341	 2848| \end{lemma}
   342	 2849| 
   343	 2850| \begin{proof}
   344	 2851|   Fourier uniqueness gives $\mu(B_r) = r^\alpha\mu(B_1)$. The Gaussian
   345	 2852|   comparison in Lemma~\ref{L:phase-contractions} uses no dimension-specific
   346	 2853|   identity:
   347	 2854|   \[
   348	 2855|     \int e^{-s|\eta+\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
   349	 2856|     =\int p_{2s}^{(d)}(x)e^{i\eta\cdot x}\Gamma(\ud x)
   350	 2857|     \le\int e^{-s|\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi).
   351	 2858|   \]
   352	 2859|   Evenness gives a real integral, and physical nonnegativity gives the
   353	 2860|   inequality. Integrating against $e^{-\rho^2s}\ud s$ and using radial spectral
   354	 2861|   homogeneity yields
   355	 2862|   \[
   356	 2863|     \sup_\eta\int\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{\rho^2+|\eta+\xi|^2}
   357	 2864|     \le R_\alpha\rho^{\alpha-2}.
   358	 2865|   \]
   359	 2866|   No exclusion of a physical origin atom is used.
   360	 2867| 
   361	 2868|   Gaussian isometry and unnormalized spatial Plancherel give
   362	 2869|   \[
   363	 2870|     \sum_m\|A_\rho^{-1/2}M_{e_m}f\|_2^2
   364	 2871|     =\frac1{(2\pi)^d}\int|\widehat{f}(\eta)|^2
   365	 2872|     \left(\int\frac{e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi)}
   366	 2873|     {\rho^2+|\eta+\xi|^2}\right)\ud\eta .
   367	 2874|   \]

   369	 2876|   sub-sum. For a Fourier-band projection $S_b$, which commutes with $A_\rho$,
   370	 2877|   use $S_bA_\rho^{-1}S_b \le A_\rho^{-1}$ to obtain the same inequality for
   371	 2878|   $S_bM_{e_m}S_b$. The phase assertion on a new color follows because
   372	 2879|   $\sum_mg_m(0,M_{e_m}u)$ has squared norm given by the left side
   373	 2880|   of~\eqref{E:interval-column}, and its input is independent of this color.
   374	 2881| 
   375	 2882|   Substituting $A_\rho^{-1/2}f$ gives
   376	 2883|   \[
   377	 2884|     \sum_m(A_\rho^{-1/2}M_{e_m}A_\rho^{-1/2})^2
   378	 2885|     \le R_\alpha\rho^{\alpha-4}I.
   379	 2886|   \]

   381	 2888|   agree. The normalized Hermite creation-row norm from degree $j$ to degree
   382	 2889|   $j+1$ is $\sqrt{j+1}$, and annihilation is its adjoint, as proved in
   383	 2890|   Lemma~\ref{L:fock-form}. Composition with the spatial column and addition of

   387	 2894|   nonnegativity. Thus, $R_\alpha$ is the only covariance quantity in these
   388	 2895|   estimates. No angular bound or unsmoothed multiplication norm has been
   389	 2896|   absorbed into a constant. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:interval-contractions}.
   390	 2897| \end{proof}

    68	def hermR (n : ℕ) : ℝ[X] := (hermite n).map (Int.castRingHom ℝ)

    74	`He_{n+1}' = (n+1) He_n`. -/
    75	theorem derivative_hermite_succ : ∀ n : ℕ,
    76	    derivative (hermite (n + 1)) = ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ[X]) * hermite n
    77	  | 0 => by simp [hermite_zero]
    78	  | n + 1 => by
    79	    have ih := derivative_hermite_succ n
    80	    rw [hermite_succ (n + 1), derivative_sub, derivative_mul, derivative_X, ih,
    81	      derivative_mul, derivative_natCast, zero_mul, zero_add]
    82	    rw [hermite_succ n]; push_cast; ring
    83	
    84	/-- `He_0 = 1`. -/
    85	theorem hermR_zero : hermR 0 = 1 := by simp [hermR]

    87	/-- `He_{n+1} = x He_n - He_n'`. -/
    88	theorem hermR_succ (n : ℕ) : hermR (n + 1) = X * hermR n - derivative (hermR n) := by

   137	/-- Every real polynomial is integrable against `N(0,1)`. -/
   138	theorem integrable_eval (p : ℝ[X]) :
   139	    Integrable (fun x => p.eval x) (gaussianReal 0 1) := by
   140	  have h : (fun x => p.eval x) =
   141	      fun x => ∑ i ∈ range (p.natDegree + 1), p.coeff i * x ^ i := by
   142	    funext x; exact eval_eq_sum_range x
   143	  rw [h]

   148	def gE (p : ℝ[X]) : ℝ := ∫ x, p.eval x ∂gaussianReal 0 1

   155	theorem gE_sub (p q : ℝ[X]) : gE (p - q) = gE p - gE q := by

   159	theorem gE_C (c : ℝ) : gE (C c) = c := by simp [gE]

   162	theorem gE_X_mul (p : ℝ[X]) : gE (X * p) = gE (derivative p) := by
   163	  have h := GaussianIBP.integral_mul_eq_integral_deriv (fun x => p.eval x)
   164	    (fun x => (derivative p).eval x) (fun x => p.hasDerivAt x) (integrable_eval p)
   165	    ((integrable_eval (X * p)).congr (ae_of_all _ fun x => by simp)) (integrable_eval _)

   169	theorem gE_hermR_succ_mul (n : ℕ) (q : ℝ[X]) :
   170	    gE (hermR (n + 1) * q) = gE (hermR n * derivative q) := by
   171	  have h1 : hermR (n + 1) * q = X * (hermR n * q) - derivative (hermR n) * q := by
   172	    rw [hermR_succ]; ring

   174	    derivative_mul
   175	  rw [h1, gE_sub, gE_X_mul, h2, gE_add]; ring

   178	theorem gE_hermR_mul (n : ℕ) (q : ℝ[X]) :

   189	    simpa [h.ne] using gE_C 0
   190	  · subst h; rw [gE_hermR_mul, iterate_derivative_hermR_self, gE_C]; simp

   108	/-- A self-adjoint operator is symmetric. -/
   109	theorem symm_of_isSelfAdjoint [CompleteSpace X] {T : X →L[ℂ] X} (hT : IsSelfAdjoint T)
   110	    (u w : X) : inner ℂ (T u) w = inner ℂ u (T w) :=

   113	/-- A symmetric idempotent (an orthogonal projection, such as the band
   114	projection `S_b`) does not increase norms. -/
   115	theorem norm_proj_le {P : X →L[ℂ] X} (hPs : ∀ u w, inner ℂ (P u) w = inner ℂ u (P w))
   116	    (hPP : ∀ u, P (P u) = P u) (u : X) : ‖P u‖ ≤ ‖u‖ := by
   117	  have h : ‖P u‖ ^ 2 ≤ ‖u‖ * ‖P u‖ := by
   118	    rw [@norm_sq_eq_re_inner ℂ, hPs, hPP]
   119	    exact re_inner_le_norm _ _
   120	  rcases (norm_nonneg (P u)).eq_or_lt with h0 | h0
   121	  · rw [← h0]; exact norm_nonneg _
   122	  · nlinarith

   124	/-- Compression preserves symmetry: `P H P` is symmetric for symmetric `P, H`. -/
   125	theorem compress_symm {P T : X →L[ℂ] X} (hPs : ∀ u w, inner ℂ (P u) w = inner ℂ u (P w))
   126	    (hT : ∀ u w, inner ℂ (T u) w = inner ℂ u (T w)) (u w : X) :
   127	    inner ℂ ((P ∘L T ∘L P) u) w = inner ℂ u ((P ∘L T ∘L P) w) := by
   128	  simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply]
   129	  rw [hPs, hT, hPs]

   131	/-- **Compression by `S_b`** (main TeX lines 2511-2513): if `∑_i ‖H_i u‖² ≤ c‖u‖²`
   132	with `c ≥ 0` and `P` is a symmetric idempotent, then the same bound holds for
   133	`P H_i P`. -/
   134	theorem fockColumn_compress {H : Fin m → X →L[ℂ] X} {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 ≤ c)
   135	    (hc : FockColumn H c) {P : X →L[ℂ] X} (hPs : ∀ u w, inner ℂ (P u) w = inner ℂ u (P w))
   136	    (hPP : ∀ u, P (P u) = P u) : FockColumn (fun i => P ∘L H i ∘L P) c := by
   137	  intro u
   138	  calc ∑ i, ‖(P ∘L H i ∘L P) u‖ ^ 2 ≤ ∑ i, ‖H i (P u)‖ ^ 2 :=
   139	        Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _)
   140	          (norm_proj_le hPs hPP _) 2
   141	    _ ≤ c * ‖P u‖ ^ 2 := hc (P u)
   142	    _ ≤ c * ‖u‖ ^ 2 := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
   143	          (pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_proj_le hPs hPP u) 2) hc0

   147	theorem fock_const_eq (N : ℕ) {R ρ alpha : ℝ} (hR : 0 ≤ R) (hρ : 0 < ρ) :
   148	    2 * √((N : ℝ) + 1) * √(R * ρ ^ (alpha - 4)) =
   149	      StaticPhaseCauchy.fockD N R * ρ ^ (alpha / 2 - 2) := by
   150	  have h : √(ρ ^ (alpha - 4)) = ρ ^ (alpha / 2 - 2) := by
   151	    rw [Real.sqrt_eq_rpow, ← Real.rpow_mul hρ.le]; congr 1; ring
   152	  rw [Real.sqrt_mul hR, h, StaticPhaseCauchy.fockD]; ring

   156	/-- **`L:fock-form`, general form** (`E:fock-sandwich`, main TeX lines
   157	2484-2488).  Let `H_1, …, H_m` be symmetric operators on `X` with the column
   158	bound `FockColumn H (R ρ^{α-4})` (named input; `R ≥ 0`, `ρ > 0`), and `P` a
   159	symmetric idempotent (the band projection `S_b`).  Then for every `N`, on
   160	coefficient vectors `v` of Hermite degree at most `N`, the operator
   161	`B = P_N (∑_i g_i ⊗ P H_i P) P_N` satisfies
   162	(i) `∑_{|k| ≤ N} ‖(B v)_k‖² ≤ (d_N ρ^{α/2-2})² ∑_{|k| ≤ N} ‖v_k‖²`;
   163	(ii) the same bound in Gaussian `L²(γ_m; X)` for the expansions `iota`, with
   164	integrability; (iii) `B` is symmetric on degrees `≤ N`. -/
   165	theorem fock_form {R ρ alpha : ℝ} (hR : 0 ≤ R) (hρ : 0 < ρ) (H : Fin m → X →L[ℂ] X)
   166	    (hH : ∀ i u w, inner ℂ (H i u) w = inner ℂ u (H i w))
   167	    (hcol : FockColumn H (R * ρ ^ (alpha - 4))) (P : X →L[ℂ] X)
   168	    (hPs : ∀ u w, inner ℂ (P u) w = inner ℂ u (P w)) (hPP : ∀ u, P (P u) = P u)
   169	    (N : ℕ) {v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X} (hv : Supp N v) :
   170	    ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, ‖fieldOp (fun i => P ∘L H i ∘L P) v k‖ ^ 2 ≤
   171	        (StaticPhaseCauchy.fockD N R * ρ ^ (alpha / 2 - 2)) ^ 2 * ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, ‖v k‖ ^ 2 ∧
   172	      Integrable (fun x => ‖iota N (fieldOp (fun i => P ∘L H i ∘L P) v) x‖ ^ 2)
   173	        (GaussianIBP.stdPi m) ∧
   174	      ∫ x, ‖iota N (fieldOp (fun i => P ∘L H i ∘L P) v) x‖ ^ 2 ∂GaussianIBP.stdPi m ≤
   175	        (StaticPhaseCauchy.fockD N R * ρ ^ (alpha / 2 - 2)) ^ 2 *
   176	          ∫ x, ‖iota N v x‖ ^ 2 ∂GaussianIBP.stdPi m ∧
   177	      ∀ w : (Fin m → ℕ) → X, Supp N w →
   178	        ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, inner ℂ (fieldOp (fun i => P ∘L H i ∘L P) v k) (w k) =
   179	          ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, inner ℂ (v k) (fieldOp (fun i => P ∘L H i ∘L P) w k) := by
   180	  have hc0 : 0 ≤ R * ρ ^ (alpha - 4) := mul_nonneg hR (Real.rpow_nonneg hρ.le _)
   181	  have hsym : ∀ i u w, inner ℂ ((P ∘L H i ∘L P) u) w = inner ℂ u ((P ∘L H i ∘L P) w) :=
   182	    fun i => compress_symm hPs (hH i)
   183	  have hcomp := fockColumn_compress hc0 hcol hPs hPP
   184	  have hconst := fock_const_eq N (alpha := alpha) hR hρ
   185	  obtain ⟨hint, hb⟩ := gaussian_field_bound_trunc N _ hsym hc0 hcomp hv
   186	  refine ⟨?_, hint, ?_, fun w hw => fieldOp_symm_trunc N _ hsym hv hw⟩
   187	  · rw [← hconst]; exact fieldOp_bound_trunc N _ hsym hc0 hcomp hv
   188	  · rw [← hconst]; exact hb

  1773	\begin{proposition}[Mild construction from the fixed-order limits]
  1774	  \label{P:mild-construction}
  1775	  Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, the series $u(t,x) = \sum_{n\ge0}X_n(t,x)$ is
  1776	  a mild solution in~\cite{chen:author2026:time-dependency}*{Definition~2.1 and
  1777	  (2.12), pp.~9--10}. More precisely, for each $t > 0$ and $x \in \R^d$,
  1778	  \begin{equation}\label{E:mild-construction}
  1779	    \lim_{\epsilon,\delta\downarrow0}
  1780	    \int_0^t\int_{\R^d}G(t-s,x-\ud y)
  1781	    u(s,y)W_{\epsilon,\delta}(s,y)\ud s
  1782	    =u(t,x)-1\quad\text{in }L^2(\Omega).
  1783	  \end{equation}
  1784	  The limit allows arbitrary relative rates of the two widths. In dimension
  1785	  three the Green-width limit precedes the noise-width limit. No uniqueness
  1786	  assertion is made.
  1787	\end{proposition}
  1788	
  1789	For $d = 3$ we read the source's generalized-integrand definition using its
  1790	Green regularization, with the random factor held fixed. The proof below
  1791	establishes that limit for the product $uW_{\epsilon,\delta}$.
  1792	
  1793	\begin{proof}
  1794	  Let $\mathscr{P}_{\le n}$ be the closed Gaussian polynomial space of total
  1795	  degree at most $n$, generated by all the coupled source fields. It includes
  1796	  all lower-degree contractions. The fixed-width terminal integrals lie in this
  1797	  space, by their Bochner construction; their fixed-order $L^2$ limits $X_n$ do
  1798	  too.
  1799	
  1800	  We first record an elementary multiplication bound on these spaces. If $H$ is
  1801	  any centered linear Gaussian variable and $F \in \mathscr{P}_{\le n}$, then
  1802	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupied-multiplication}
  1803	    \|HF\|_2\le2\sqrt{n+1}\,\|H\|_2\|F\|_2.
  1804	  \end{equation}
  1805	  If $H = 0$ the assertion is immediate. Otherwise take $H/\|H\|_2$ as the first
  1806	  coordinate of an orthonormal Gaussian basis. On normalized Hermite polynomials
  1807	  its creation and annihilation operators have norms at most $\sqrt{n+1}$ and
  1808	  $\sqrt n$ on total degrees at most $n$: the squared coefficient sums have
  1809	  respective weights $a_1+1 \le n+1$ and $a_1 \le n$. Their sum proves the bound
  1810	  for finite-coordinate polynomials. Approximation in the degree-closed space
  1811	  proves it for $F$ as well. Indeed, the products of an approximating sequence
  1812	  are $L^2$ Cauchy by this bound; subsequences converging almost surely identify
  1813	  their limit with $HF$. This also proves the closedness of multiplication
  1814	  needed below. The argument allows $F$ to depend on $H$.
  1815	
  2461	  The phase operator itself is the exponential of the bounded block generator
  2462	  with rows $(0,1)$ and $(-L,0)$. It is entire in $z$; the intermediate square
  2463	  roots are used to estimate it, not to impose a branch-dependent definition of
  2464	  that entire operator. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:complex-phase}.
  2465	\end{proof}
  2466	
  2467	We use the standard Gaussian creation and annihilation algebra; see
  2468	Janson~\cite{janson:97:gaussian}*{Section~13.2, Theorem~13.7, pp.~200--201}.
  2469	The following calculation records the normalization used for the finite
  2470	occupation spaces in this argument.

  2472	\begin{lemma}[Gaussian cutoff form bound]\label{L:fock-form}
  2473	  Retain the covariance and $R_\alpha$ of Section~\ref{S:static-phase}. Fix
  2474	  $\epsilon > 0$. Represent the smoothed real field on independent standard
  2475	  Gaussian coordinates as $W_\epsilon(x) = \sum_{i\ge1}g_i e_i(x)$ in
  2476	  $L^2(\Omega)$. Let $P_N$ be projection onto Gaussian Hermite degrees at most
  2477	  $N$, and $S_b$ spatial Fourier projection onto $|\eta| \le b$. For finite $m$,
  2478	  on their joint range set
  2479	  \[
  2480	    B_{N,m,b}=P_NS_b\Big(\sum_{i=1}^m g_i M_{e_i}\Big)S_bP_N,\qquad
  2481	    A_\rho=\rho^2-\Delta .
  2482	  \]
  2483	  These are bounded selfadjoint operators and, uniformly in $\epsilon,m,b$,
  2484	  \begin{equation}\label{E:fock-sandwich}
  2485	    \|A_\rho^{-1/2}B_{N,m,b}A_\rho^{-1/2}\|
  2486	    \le d_N\rho^{\alpha/2-2},\qquad
  2487	    d_N=2\sqrt{N+1}\sqrt{R_\alpha}.
  2488	  \end{equation}
  2489	\end{lemma}
  2490	
  2491	\begin{proof}
  2492	  Choose an orthonormal basis of the real isonormal space, which is separable,
  2493	  and write $e_i(x) = \E[W_\epsilon(x)g_i]$. Then $\sum_i e_i(x)^2 =
  2494	  \Gamma_\epsilon(0) = :v_\epsilon$, and $|e_i(x)| \le \sqrt{v_\epsilon}$. Thus,
  2495	  each multiplication $M_{e_i}$ is bounded and selfadjoint. Put $H_i =
  2496	  A_\rho^{-1/2}M_{e_i}A_\rho^{-1/2}$ on spatial $L^2$. Gaussian isometry and
  2497	  spatial Plancherel give
  2498	  \[
  2499	    \sum_i\|H_i f\|_2^2
  2500	    =\frac1{(2\pi)^3}\int
  2501	    \frac{|\widehat{f}(\eta)|^2}{\rho^2+|\eta|^2}
  2502	    J_{\rho,\epsilon}(\eta)\ud\eta,\qquad
  2503	    J_{\rho,\epsilon}(\eta)
  2504	    =\int\frac{e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi)}
  2505	    {\rho^2+|\eta+\xi|^2}.
  2506	  \]
  2507	  This is the covariance calculation for $A_\rho^{-1/2}W_\epsilon
  2508	  A_\rho^{-1/2}f$. By Lemma~\ref{L:phase-contractions}, $J_{\rho,\epsilon} \le
  2509	  R_\alpha\rho^{\alpha-2}$. Therefore, $\sum_i H_i^2 \le
  2510	  R_\alpha\rho^{\alpha-4}I$ in quadratic forms. Finite sums have the same upper
  2511	  bound. Compression to $S_b$ preserves it: for selfadjoint $H_i$,
  2512	  $(S_bH_iS_b)^2 \le S_bH_i^2S_b$ on its range. Both row and column variances
  2513	  are the same, since these operators are selfadjoint.
  2514	
  2515	  For completeness, use normalized Hermite polynomials, so multiplication by
  2516	  $g_i$ is $a_i^*+a_i$, with $g_i h_k =
  2517	  \sqrt{k_i+1}\,h_{k+e_i}+\sqrt{k_i}\,h_{k-e_i}$. On degree $k$, the row map
  2518	  $(v_i)\mapsto\sum_i a_i^*v_i$ has norm $\sqrt{k+1}$: its product with its
  2519	  adjoint is $\sum_i a_i^*a_i = (k+1)I$ on degree $k+1$. Composing with the

  2527	\end{proof}

     6	
     7	def bump (i : C) (d : C → Nat) : C → Nat :=
     8	  fun c => d c + if c = i then 1 else 0
     9	
    10	def counts : List (C × B) → C → Nat
    11	  | [] => fun _ => 0
    12	  | (i, _) :: w => bump i (counts w)
    13	
    14	def raw (J : C → V → V) (F : B → V → V) (v₀ : V) : List (C × B) → V
    15	  | [] => v₀
    16	  | (i, b) :: w => F b (J i (raw J F v₀ w))
    17	
    18	def cut (P : V → V) (J : C → V → V) (F : B → V → V)
    19	    (v₀ : V) : List (C × B) → V
    20	  | [] => v₀
    21	  | (i, b) :: w => F b (P (J i (P (cut P J F v₀ w))))
    22	
    23	theorem raw_support
    24	    (Good : (C → Nat) → V → Prop)
    25	    (J : C → V → V) (F : B → V → V) (v₀ : V)
    26	    (hv₀ : Good (fun _ => 0) v₀)
    27	    (hJ : ∀ d i v, Good d v → Good (bump i d) (J i v))
    28	    (hF : ∀ d b v, Good d v → Good d (F b v))
    29	    (w : List (C × B)) : Good (counts w) (raw J F v₀ w) := by
    30	  induction w with
    31	  | nil => exact hv₀
    32	  | cons a w ih =>
    33	    exact hF _ a.2 _ (hJ _ a.1 _ ih)
    34	
    35	theorem cut_eq_raw
    36	    (Good : (C → Nat) → V → Prop)
    37	    (J : C → V → V) (F : B → V → V) (P : V → V)
    38	    (v₀ : V) (N : C → Nat)
    39	    (hv₀ : Good (fun _ => 0) v₀)
    40	    (hJ : ∀ d i v, Good d v → Good (bump i d) (J i v))
    41	    (hF : ∀ d b v, Good d v → Good d (F b v))
    42	    (hP : ∀ d v, (∀ c, d c ≤ N c) → Good d v → P v = v)
    43	    (w : List (C × B)) (hN : ∀ c, counts w c ≤ N c) :
    44	    cut P J F v₀ w = raw J F v₀ w := by
    45	  induction w with
    46	  | nil => rfl
    47	  | cons a w ih =>
    48	    have hs : ∀ c, counts w c ≤ N c := by
    49	      intro c
    50	      have hc := hN c
    51	      simp only [counts, bump] at hc
    52	      omega
    53	    have hw := raw_support Good J F v₀ hv₀ hJ hF w
    54	    have hp₀ := hP (counts w) (raw J F v₀ w) hs hw
    55	    have hp₁ := hP (bump a.1 (counts w)) (J a.1 (raw J F v₀ w))
    56	      hN (hJ _ _ _ hw)
    57	    change F a.2 (P (J a.1 (P (cut P J F v₀ w)))) =
    58	      F a.2 (J a.1 (raw J F v₀ w))
    59	    rw [ih hs, hp₀, hp₁]

     6	-- Coefficients in the unnormalized probabilists' Hermite basis:
     7	-- x He_n = He_(n+1) + n He_(n-1). This defines the finite recurrence;
     8	-- no assertion about Gaussian L² or polynomial realization is imported.
     9	private def vacuum (n : Nat) : Nat := if n = 0 then 1 else 0
    10	private def insert (_ : Unit) (p : Nat → Nat) (n : Nat) : Nat :=
    11	  (if n = 0 then 0 else p (n-1)) + (n+1) * p (n+1)
    12	private def frame (_ : Unit) (p : Nat → Nat) := p
    13	private def project (N : Nat) (p : Nat → Nat) (n : Nat) :=
    14	  if n ≤ N then p n else 0
    15	private def Good (d : Unit → Nat) (p : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
    16	  ∀ n, d () < n → p n = 0
    17	
    18	private theorem vacuum_good : Good (fun _ => 0) vacuum := by
    19	  intro n hn
    20	  simp only [vacuum]
    21	  split <;> omega
    22	
    23	private theorem insert_good (d : Unit → Nat) (i : Unit) (p : Nat → Nat)
    24	    (hp : Good d p) : Good (bump i d) (insert i p) := by
    25	  intro n hn
    26	  have hi : i = () := by cases i; rfl
    27	  subst i
    28	  simp [bump] at hn
    29	  have h₁ : p (n-1) = 0 := hp _ (by omega)
    30	  have h₂ : p (n+1) = 0 := hp _ (by omega)
    31	  simp [insert, h₁, h₂]
    32	
    33	private theorem frame_good (d : Unit → Nat) (b : Unit) (p : Nat → Nat)
    34	    (hp : Good d p) : Good d (frame b p) := hp
    35	
    36	private theorem project_fixes (N : Nat) (d : Unit → Nat) (p : Nat → Nat)
    37	    (hd : ∀ c, d c ≤ N) (hp : Good d p) : project N p = p := by
    38	  funext n
    39	  simp only [project]
    40	  split
    41	  · rfl
    42	  · exact (hp n (by have h := hd (); omega)).symm
    43	
    44	private theorem count_length (w : List (Unit × Unit)) : counts w () = w.length := by
    45	  induction w with
    46	  | nil => rfl
    47	  | cons a w ih =>
    48	    have ha : a.1 = () := by cases a with | mk i b => cases i; rfl
    49	    simp [counts, bump, ha, ih]
    50	
    51	-- Actual recurrence consumer, arbitrary word length and cutoff; not a third
    52	-- public claim and not the analytic Hermite/Hilbert realization theorem.
    53	example (w : List (Unit × Unit)) (N : Nat) (hN : w.length ≤ N) :
    54	    cut (project N) insert frame vacuum w = raw insert frame vacuum w := by
    55	  apply cut_eq_raw Good insert frame (project N) vacuum (fun _ => N)
    56	    vacuum_good insert_good frame_good (project_fixes N) w
    57	  intro c
    58	  cases c
    59	  simpa only [count_length] using hN

    62	example : cut (project 4) insert frame vacuum [ ((),()), ((),()), ((),()), ((),()) ] 0 = 3 := by

    66	example : raw insert frame vacuum [ ((),()), ((),()) ] 2 = 1 := by decide

    68	example : raw insert frame vacuum [ ((),()), ((),()) ] 0 = 1 := by decide

  2043	\section{A static phase estimate at first variance order}
  2044	\label{S:static-phase}
  2045	
  2046	A time-block argument would have to carry both position and velocity. We
  2047	establish a uniform estimate for the first variance coefficient with arbitrary
  2048	deterministic initial phase. The covariance may be any member of the original
  2049	three-dimensional class; no endpoint representation is assumed. The estimate
  2050	below is not an all-order propagator bound.
  2051	
  2052	
  2053	
  2054	Let $0 < \alpha < 2$, and let $\Gamma$ be a nonnegative, even, positive-definite
  2055	tempered Radon covariance on $\R^3$, satisfying $\Gamma(rA) =
  2056	r^{3-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$. Its spectral convention is $\Gamma = \int e^{i\xi\cdot
  2057	x}\mu(\ud\xi)$. Put
  2058	\begin{equation}\label{E:phase-constants}
  2059	  \begin{split}
  2060	    V&=\mu(B_1),\qquad M=\Gamma(B_1),\qquad
  2061	    R_\alpha=\frac{\alpha\pi V}{2\sin(\pi\alpha/2)},\\
  2062	    c_\Gamma&=\frac{(3-\alpha)M}{4\pi},\qquad
  2063	    b_\alpha=2^\alpha+\frac{3^{2-\alpha}}{2-\alpha},\qquad
  2064	    D_\Gamma=c_\Gamma b_\alpha.
  2065	  \end{split}
  2066	\end{equation}
  2067	Here $B_1$ is the open unit ball in the relevant variable. The physical mass $M$
  2068	and the spectral mass $V$ are not identified. Let $p_\epsilon$ be the Brownian
  2069	Gaussian density with covariance $\epsilon I$, and set $\Gamma_\epsilon =
  2070	p_{2\epsilon}*\Gamma$.
  2071	
  2072	\begin{lemma}[Two static contraction bounds]\label{L:phase-contractions}
  2073	  For $\lambda > 0$, $q \in \R^3$, $a > 0$, and $\epsilon > 0$,
  2074	  \begin{align}
  2075	    \int_{\R^3}\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{\lambda^2+|q+\xi|^2}
  2076	    &\le R_\alpha\lambda^{\alpha-2},
  2077	    \label{E:phase-resolvent}\\
  2078	    \left|T_\epsilon(a,q)\right|
  2079	    &\le D_\Gamma a^{1-\alpha},
  2080	    \label{E:phase-trace}\\
  2081	    T_\epsilon(a,q)
  2082	    &:=\int_{\R^3}e^{iq\cdot x}\Gamma_\epsilon(x)G_a(\ud x)
  2083	    =\int_{\R^3}\widehat{G}_a(q+\xi)e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2}
  2084	    \mu(\ud\xi).\nonumber
  2085	  \end{align}
  2086	\end{lemma}

  2090	  there is no origin atom. For $s > 0$, Schwartz Fourier pairing yields
  2091	  \[
  2092	    \int e^{-s|q+\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
  2093	    =\int p_{2s}(x)e^{iq\cdot x}\Gamma(\ud x)
  2094	    \le\int p_{2s}(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
  2095	    =\int e^{-s|\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi).
  2096	  \]
  2097	  The integrals are finite. Evenness makes the middle integral real, and
  2098	  nonnegativity of $\Gamma$ gives the inequality. Multiply by $e^{-\lambda^2s}$
  2099	  and integrate in $s$. Nonnegative Tonelli on the spectral side gives the
  2100	  resolvent comparison. At $q = 0$ its value is
  2101	  \[
  2102	    \alpha V\int_0^\infty\frac{r^{\alpha-1}}{\lambda^2+r^2}\ud r
  2103	    =R_\alpha\lambda^{\alpha-2}.
  2104	  \]

  2106	
  2107	  Since $\mu$ is tempered, its Gaussian weighting is finite. Fourier Fubini
  2108	  therefore gives the identity for $T_\epsilon$. The measure
  2109	  $\Gamma_\epsilon(x)G_a(\ud x)$ is finite and nonnegative, whence
  2110	  $|T_\epsilon(a,q)| \le T_\epsilon(a,0)$. The radial distribution function of
  2111	  $\Gamma$ is $\Gamma(B_r) = Mr^{3-\alpha}$. Thus, for every nonnegative radial
  2112	  Schwartz function $F$,

  2115	    =(3-\alpha)M\int_0^\infty F(r)r^{2-\alpha}\ud r
  2116	    =c_\Gamma\int_{\R^3}F(x)|x|^{-\alpha}\ud x.

  2121	    T_\epsilon(a,0)
  2122	    =c_\Gamma[p_{2\epsilon}*(G_a*|\cdot|^{-\alpha})](0)
  2123	    \le c_\Gamma\sup_z(G_a*|\cdot|^{-\alpha})(z).
  2124	  \]

  2126	  integration over its normal coordinate gives, for $r > 0$,
  2127	  \[
  2128	    (G_a*|\cdot|^{-\alpha})(z)
  2129	    =\frac{(a+r)^{2-\alpha}-|a-r|^{2-\alpha}}
  2130	    {2r(2-\alpha)}.
  2131	  \]

  2533	  Gaussian coordinates, grouped by color $i$, and let $\mathscr{X}$ be a complex
  2534	  Hilbert space. On Gaussian polynomials with coefficients in $\mathscr{X}$ set

  2537	  \]

  2539	  bounded operators acting only on $\mathscr{X}$. Fix a word $i_1,\ldots,i_n$,
  2540	  and let $r_i$ be the number of its occurrences of color $i$. If $N_i \ge r_i$
  2541	  and $P$ projects each color onto total Hermite degree at most $N_i$, then, for
  2542	  every $v \in \mathscr{X}$,
  2543	  \begin{equation}\label{E:finite-word-cutoff}
  2544	    \begin{split}
  2545	      &(I\otimes F_n)(PJ_{i_n}P)(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
  2546	      (PJ_{i_1}P)(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v)\\
  2547	      &\qquad=(I\otimes F_n)J_{i_n}(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
  2548	      J_{i_1}(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v).
  2549	    \end{split}
  2550	  \end{equation}

  2552	  whenever the displayed vector integrals exist.

  2557	  $h_{\boldsymbol a}$ to $\sqrt{a_{ij}+1}\,h_{\boldsymbol a+e_{ij}}

  2560	  other color degrees unchanged. The operators $I\otimes F_l$ leave every

  2562	  word therefore has color-$i$ degree at most $r_i(l) = |\{j\le l:i_j=i\}| \le

  2797	
  2798	These estimates concern individual static phase and interaction maps. Their
  2799	summability alone does not identify the evolution driven by overlapping interval
  2800	fields. The coefficient argument in Section~\ref{S:interval-upper} supplies the
  2801	separate estimate needed for that evolution.
  2802	
  2803	\section{Interval fields and the full upper bound}
  2804	\label{S:interval-upper}
  2805	
  2806	The intrinsic constant is identified independently in
  2807	Theorem~\ref{T:intrinsic-second-moment}.
  2808	
  2809	Write
  2810	\[
  2811	  \nu=3-\alpha>1,\qquad
  2812	  \beta=4-\alpha-\alpha_0>2,\qquad p=2-\alpha_0>1.
  2813	\]
  2814	Thus, $\beta-\nu = 1-\alpha_0 > 0$. In this section the spatial dimension is any
  2815	admissible $d \in \{1,2,3\}$. The spatial covariance is the nonnegative, even,
  2816	positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$, with scaling $\Gamma(rA) =
  2817	r^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$ and spectral convention $\Gamma = \int e^{i\xi\cdot
  2818	x}\mu(\ud\xi)$. This includes $\Gamma = \delta_0$ when $d = \alpha = 1$. Set
  2819	\[
  2820	  R_\alpha=\frac{\alpha\pi\mu(B_1)}{2\sin(\pi\alpha/2)},\qquad
  2821	  A_\rho=\rho^2-\Delta,\qquad
  2822	  \|(f,g)\|_\rho^2=\|f\|_2^2+\|A_\rho^{-1/2}g\|_2^2.
  2823	\]
  2824	Complex Hilbert inner products are linear in the first slot.
  2825	
  2826	\subsection{Contractions and complex phase estimates}
  2827	
  2828	\begin{lemma}[Dimension-independent Gaussian contractions]
  2829	  \label{L:interval-contractions}
  2830	  Uniformly in positive spatial smoothing and in finite Gaussian-mode and
  2831	  spatial Fourier-band cutoffs,
  2832	  \begin{equation}\label{E:interval-column}
  2833	    \sum_m\|A_\rho^{-1/2}M_{e_m}f\|_2^2
  2834	    \le R_\alpha\rho^{\alpha-2}\|f\|_2^2.
  2835	  \end{equation}
  2836	  Here $W_\epsilon(x) = \sum_m g_me_m(x)$ is an orthonormal-coordinate
  2837	  representation of $W(p_\epsilon(x-\cdot))$, whose covariance is
  2838	  $\Gamma_\epsilon = p_{2\epsilon}*\Gamma$. Consequently, on a Gaussian color
  2839	  that is initially in its vacuum, the phase insertion
  2840	  $(u,v)\mapsto(0,W_\epsilon u)$ has norm at most
  2841	  $\sqrt{R_\alpha}\rho^{(\alpha-2)/2}$ into its Gaussian $L^2$ phase. With
  2842	  Hermite degree of this color truncated at $N$, its sandwiched field has
  2843	  operator norm at most
  2844	  \begin{equation}\label{E:interval-fock}
  2845	    2\sqrt{N+1}\sqrt{R_\alpha}\rho^{\alpha/2-2}.
  2846	  \end{equation}
  2847	  Both statements remain valid tensoring with any other Hilbert factor.
  2848	\end{lemma}
  2849	
  2850	\begin{proof}
  2851	  Fourier uniqueness gives $\mu(B_r) = r^\alpha\mu(B_1)$. The Gaussian
  2852	  comparison in Lemma~\ref{L:phase-contractions} uses no dimension-specific
  2853	  identity:
  2854	  \[
  2855	    \int e^{-s|\eta+\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
  2856	    =\int p_{2s}^{(d)}(x)e^{i\eta\cdot x}\Gamma(\ud x)
  2857	    \le\int e^{-s|\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi).
  2858	  \]
  2859	  Evenness gives a real integral, and physical nonnegativity gives the
  2860	  inequality. Integrating against $e^{-\rho^2s}\ud s$ and using radial spectral
  2861	  homogeneity yields
  2862	  \[
  2863	    \sup_\eta\int\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{\rho^2+|\eta+\xi|^2}
  2864	    \le R_\alpha\rho^{\alpha-2}.
  2865	  \]
  2866	  No exclusion of a physical origin atom is used.
  2867	
  2868	  Gaussian isometry and unnormalized spatial Plancherel give
  2869	  \[
  2870	    \sum_m\|A_\rho^{-1/2}M_{e_m}f\|_2^2
  2871	    =\frac1{(2\pi)^d}\int|\widehat{f}(\eta)|^2
  2872	    \left(\int\frac{e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi)}
  2873	    {\rho^2+|\eta+\xi|^2}\right)\ud\eta .
  2874	  \]
  2875	  This proves~\eqref{E:interval-column}. A finite mode sum is a positive
  2876	  sub-sum. For a Fourier-band projection $S_b$, which commutes with $A_\rho$,
  2877	  use $S_bA_\rho^{-1}S_b \le A_\rho^{-1}$ to obtain the same inequality for
  2878	  $S_bM_{e_m}S_b$. The phase assertion on a new color follows because
  2879	  $\sum_mg_m(0,M_{e_m}u)$ has squared norm given by the left side
  2880	  of~\eqref{E:interval-column}, and its input is independent of this color.
  2881	
  2882	  Substituting $A_\rho^{-1/2}f$ gives
  2883	  \[
  2884	    \sum_m(A_\rho^{-1/2}M_{e_m}A_\rho^{-1/2})^2
  2885	    \le R_\alpha\rho^{\alpha-4}I.
  2886	  \]
  2887	  These spatial sandwiches are selfadjoint, so their row and column variances
  2888	  agree. The normalized Hermite creation-row norm from degree $j$ to degree
  2889	  $j+1$ is $\sqrt{j+1}$, and annihilation is its adjoint, as proved in
  2890	  Lemma~\ref{L:fock-form}. Composition with the spatial column and addition of
  2891	  the two parts prove~\eqref{E:interval-fock}. The same positive operator
  2892	  identities hold with an identity on every other Hilbert factor. The
  2893	  calculation used only the radial mass $\mu(B_1)$, homogeneity and physical
  2894	  nonnegativity. Thus, $R_\alpha$ is the only covariance quantity in these
  2895	  estimates. No angular bound or unsmoothed multiplication norm has been
  2896	  absorbed into a constant. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:interval-contractions}.
  2897	\end{proof}

   826	+## HermiteFock (whole result)
   827	+
   828	+A foundation with no manuscript label of its own; everything is proved and
   829	+nothing is supplied. It is the finite Gaussian Fock layer used in
   830	+`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420` (main TeX):
   831	+the Fock half of the proof of `L:fock-form` (lines 2515-2526), the Fock
   832	+sentences of the proof of `L:interval-contractions` (lines 2887-2891), the
   833	+phase insertion on a color in its vacuum (lines 2838-2841 and 2878-2880),
   834	+and the Hermite step of `E:occupied-multiplication` (lines 1805-1810). The
   835	+TeX cites Janson (lines 2467-2468) for the creation and annihilation
   836	+algebra; this module proves what is used.
   837	+
   838	+Model (decision 5 of wave L9). The Gaussian `L^2` space with values in a
   839	+complex inner product space `X` is represented by coefficient vectors
   840	+`(Fin m -> N) -> X`, indexed by multi-indices, restricted to total degree
   841	+at most `N` (`degLE m N`; `Supp N v` says `v` vanishes above degree `N`).
   842	+The expansion `iota N v (x) = sum_(|k| <= N) h_k(x) v_k` in the normalized
   843	+Hermite functions of `GaussianHermite` links the two pictures: it is an
   844	+isometry into `L^2(stdPi m; X)` (`integral_norm_sq_iota`; `stdPi m` is the
   845	+law of `m` independent standard Gaussians), multiplication by `x_i` is
   846	+`a_i^* + a_i` on coefficients (`coord_smul_iota`), and `sum_i x_i H_i` is
   847	+the field operator `fieldOp H` (`sum_coord_smul_iota`). No tensor-product
   848	+inner product is used: the "other Hilbert factor" of the TeX is `X` itself,
   849	+and the spatial operators `H_i` are continuous linear maps of `X`. The TeX
   850	+rotates `H/||H||` to a first coordinate (line 1805); the general column
   851	+form with operators `H_i` makes that step unnecessary.
   852	+
   853	+Formalized. The annihilation and creation operators
   854	+`(a_i v)_k = sqrt(k_i+1) v_(k+e_i)`, `(a_i^* v)_k = sqrt(k_i) v_(k-e_i)`,
   855	+the number identity `sum_i a_i^* a_i = |k|`, and the finite adjoint
   856	+identity between `a_i` and `a_i^*`. The creation row from degrees `<= N` to
   857	+degrees `<= N+1` has norm at most `sqrt(N+1)` (`creRow_bound`), attained on
   858	+`u_i = a_i w` for `w` of exact degree `N+1` (`creRow_attained`). For
   859	+symmetric `H_1, ..., H_m` with the column bound
   860	+`sum_i ||H_i u||^2 <= c ||u||^2`, `c >= 0` (hypotheses of these lemmas, not
   861	+manuscript inputs here), the field operator `sum_i (a_i^* + a_i) (x) H_i`
   862	+maps degrees `<= N` to degrees `<= N+1` with norm at most
   863	+`2 sqrt(N+1) sqrt(c)` (`fieldOp_bound`), the same after truncation to
   864	+degrees `<= N` (`fieldOp_bound_trunc`), the truncated operator is symmetric
   865	+(`fieldOp_symm_trunc`), and both bounds hold in Gaussian `L^2` with
   866	+integrability (`gaussian_field_bound`, `gaussian_field_bound_trunc`).
   867	+Vacuum insertion: `E||sum_i g_i w_i||^2 = sum_i ||w_i||^2`
   868	+(`vacuum_insertion_isometry`).
   869	+
   870	+Route difference. The TeX bounds the annihilation part as the adjoint of
   871	+the creation part (line 2522); Lean uses the same adjoint relation through
   872	+the finite identity `sum_inner_ann` and Cauchy-Schwarz, which gives the
   873	+annihilation bound `(N+1) c` rather than the TeX's `N c` (line 1808 states
   874	+`sqrt(n)` for the annihilation norm). The constant `4(N+1)c` of the sum does
   875	+not need the sharper value.
   876	+
   877	+Junk values. The truncated subtraction `k - e_i` occurs only multiplied by
   878	+`sqrt(k_i)`, which vanishes exactly when it truncates; `c >= 0` is a
   879	+hypothesis where it is used; every integral conclusion includes
   880	+integrability. Coefficient vectors are arbitrary functions; only their
   881	+values in degrees `<= N` (or `<= N+1`) enter the stated sums.
   882	+
   883	+Not formalized here: the full Gaussian `L^2` space, infinitely many

884	+coordinates, the closed polynomial spaces and unbounded number operators.
   885	+
   886	+Refutations (`refutations/hermite-fock/`): `CreRowConstant` (the constant
   887	+`N` in place of `N+1` in `creRow_bound` fails at the vacuum), `NumberOrder`
   888	+(`|k| + 1` in place of `|k|` in `number_identity`) and `VacuumSquareOfSum`
   889	+(`(sum_i ||w_i||)^2` in place of `sum_i ||w_i||^2` in
   890	+`vacuum_insertion_isometry`).
